title: Tests do not write to shared live state

facts.note: Applies to ALL Bun test code (any file the Bun test runner executes, or code inside test/describe/it blocks), regardless of file name and regardless of whether the test is new or pre-existing. A test-context observer (runner config / test-block detection) is needed for full coverage.
NON-EXHAUSTIVE examples used only as a fast pre-filter for test code; a test in a differently named file is still in scope via file_kind.
Bun realization; Python sibling patterns do not apply.
Detector finding over all test code (existing and changed): `process.env.X =` assignments and write-family fs calls with a literal path outside allowed temp/fixture scopes.

values: write-family fs call in test code
facts.note: Optional diff-level observer used only as an optimization to surface new violations early; it does NOT restrict applicability — pre-existing tests that mutate env or write to live paths are equally in scope.

fires: Any test assigns `process.env.SOME_VAR = ...`, for whatever purpose (configuration, feature flags, setup, or anything else).
Any test calls a write-family fs function (write, append, mkdir, rm, etc.) with a literal path outside any temp/fixture directory, for whatever purpose.
An existing (unchanged) test already contains such a mutation or write when the suite or file is checked.
doesNotFire: A test only reads files or reads `process.env`.
A test writes to a literal path containing `tmpdir`, `/tmp`, `import.meta.dir`, `__fixtures__` or `.tmp`.
A test writes using a non-literal (computed) path — the detector cannot judge it and does not report it (detector limitation, not a permission).
Production (non-test) code sets environment variables or writes files.

given: Any test code in a Bun stack (new or existing, any file name)
when: The test mutates `process.env` or writes to the filesystem, for any purpose
then: The test MUST NOT mutate `process.env` nor write to a filesystem path outside a temp directory (shared live state: anything a later test also sees).
prefer: Scope every write to a temp directory the test owns and cleans up.
Pass configuration explicitly instead of mutating the environment, e.g. `const db = connect({ url: testUrl }); // explicit, scoped`.
avoid: Mutating `process.env` in a test, e.g. `process.env.DATABASE_URL = "postgres://live"; // leaks into every later test` — it looks local but is global, and is the most common, least obviously wrong form of pollution.
Writing to repository or other shared filesystem paths that later tests also see.
unless: The operation is a read; only the write family is in scope.
why: A polluting test does not fail; it makes a DIFFERENT test fail later, often only under a different order, with the failure pointing at the victim rather than the culprit (displaced failure). That asymmetry is why this is the family's strict rule, matching core: finding one after the fact costs days.
evidence: bun_tester_discipline_detector reports no `process.env.X =` assignments in test code.
bun_tester_discipline_detector reports no write-family fs calls whose literal path is outside the allowed temp/fixture scopes.
Suite passes regardless of test order (no displaced failures).
verifier_detail: Detector: bun_tester_discipline_detector (type: validator). Flags `process.env.X =` assignments and write-family `fs` calls whose literal path is not scoped to `tmpdir` / `/tmp` / `import.meta.dir` / `__fixtures__` / `.tmp`.
Reads are never flagged; only the write family.
A non-literal path cannot be judged by this detector and is not reported.
Severity 4; disposition strict (matching core) — fails on every finding.
audit: schema_version 1.1.0; kind rule; status active; introduced_in 0.1.0.
Realized by `bun_tester_discipline_detector`; Bun realization of the core obligation `tester.test-isolation.no-polluting-patterns`.
Stack-neutral obligation, RE-REALIZED for this stack: core's sibling detects Python bare-mode-init patterns, which do not exist here.

sharedNodes.text: strict: the rule fails on every finding; there is no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

additions.text: Test-context file_kind fact, non-exhaustive example path globs, language values, optional change-observer note, and doesNotFire for production code.
additions.justification: Source scopes the rule to 'A test' with no filename or change prerequisite; facts make that observable without narrowing it.

additions.text: Suite passes regardless of test order.
additions.justification: Derived from the displaced-failure reasoning; gives reviewers a behavioral check beyond the detector.
